history.period: 16th century; sources say 1537 (most) or 1573 (verify - minor conflict)
history.summary: One of Bengaluru's oldest temples, built in Vijayanagara style from gray granite, housing one of the world's largest monolithic Nandi statues (~15 ft tall, ~20 ft long, carved from a single granite boulder). Legend holds that a bull was devouring the groundnut crops of the surrounding fields; the idol appeared on the hill and kept growing, so a trident (soolam) was driven into its forehead to stop it - visible on the idol today. Nandi appeared in Kempe Gowda's dream asking for a temple on the hill, and the temple gave the neighbourhood its name, Basavanagudi ('bull temple' in Kannada). The small shrine with its porch is 16th-century; the present shikhara over the shrine with Shaivite figures is early 20th-century. The nearby Dodda Ganesha Gudi (Dodda Ganapathi Temple) is a short walk away. CSV town 'Bengaluru' is correct; locality Basavanagudi. Coordinates are approximate (geocoder resolved to the adjacent Dodda Ganapathi Temple on Bull Temple Road, ~100 m away - verify).

town_description: Bengaluru (Bangalore), the capital of Karnataka, is India's major technology hub, nicknamed the Silicon Valley of India, and also known as the Garden City for its parks and tree-lined avenues. Founded as a fortified town by Kempe Gowda in 1537, it blends heritage landmarks - the Bangalore Palace, Vidhana Soudha, and the 16th-century Bull Temple - with a modern metropolis. It has one of India's busiest airports and is a major domestic and international tourist gateway.
